## Glossary, for the lay reader

- **Artifact** — anything a person hands the system: a document, a
  table, an image, an audio or video file.
- **Knowledge Base ("KB")** — one body of knowledge as one graph: a
  game's rules could be one KB; a chip's instruction set another that
  someone else publishes and you simply use. Each KB keeps its own
  facts, its own history, and its own approval gate — and its own
  tailoring of the engine's conduct: the trunk ships with the engine
  at the KB's pinned version, and each KB tunes the door's voice
  (learned from its canon) and keeps its own local skills beside it.
- **World** — a context you step INTO that gathers several KBs and
  knows how they relate — nothing is melted together; the world just
  knows which KBs it uses and how to navigate them. (A world is
  itself a KB whose subject is the other KBs. Future layer.)
- **Branch** — an independent working line inside one KB: your own
  copy with its own history and gate, physically unable to touch the
  real thing, adopted only when the owner ceremonially says so.
- **Canon** — the single shared line of agreed-true facts that
  everyone's work builds on — a KB's main line.
- **Reading room** — the machinery's temporary workspace for
  understanding what was dropped; all artifacts in a submission are
  read into the same room, side by side. Disposable, never part of
  canon.
- **Pocket Universe ("Pocket")** — a private playground spanning a
  world: one invitation-ready bundle of branches, one per KB the work
  actually changes (KBs only read from are pinned, not copied),
  readable only by you until you invite someone (permissions gate who
  may *see* the Pocket; the isolation itself is the branches). Canon
  cannot be touched from inside it; exit and your view returns to
  canon, discard and nothing anywhere happened.
- **Proposal** — a bundled set of changes to canon, frozen so that what
  gets approved is exactly what gets applied.
- **Plan gate** — the first conversation: "here's how I read your
  artifact — did I read it right?"
- **Diff gate** — the second conversation: "here's exactly what would
  change in canon — approve it?"
- **Convergence loop** — the machinery re-checking and re-writing its
  own work until only questions needing human judgment remain.
- **Event log** — the permanent history of every applied change, each
  one undoable.
- **Serve** — answering questions from canon with citations, in the
  medium the evidence lives in, never inventing.

## Glossary, the working vocabulary

*The hardcore definitions — the lay glossary above stays the
gentle entry point. A knowledge base's own domain terms are
not here: they live on the graph itself
(`python -m graph terms`; every citizen carries its own doc)
and in the consuming project's own glossary.*

### The one people ask about first

**Floor** — a promise already made. Two braided uses. The **honest
floor** is the named list of everything still imperfect when work is
presented: remaining defects are classified and shown *with* the work,
never hidden under it — "an honest red beats a faked green." A
**corpus floor** is one owner-approved expectation made durable: the
check that guards it, the expectation in plain words, and the blessing
that made it a floor (a PR, a ruling), re-checked by `python -m graph
corpus` before any "done." Work may build *above* a floor; it may
never sink below one, and a floor whose guard vanishes is a loud red,
never a silence.

### Canon and the graph

**Canon** — the Neo4j canon database: the single source of truth
for everything the knowledge base asserts. Files are inputs and backups;
the graph is primary.

**Citizen** — any node that lives in canon. Facts, rulings, procedures,
quotes — if it matters, it's a citizen, queryable and owned.

**Backup / export** — `graph/export/*.jsonl`, written FROM canon,
committed to git. `restore` rebuilds the database from it alone.

**The drill** — restore from backup, then prove the database
re-serializes byte-identical. Run constantly; "DRILL PASSED" is canon's
heartbeat.

**Ground vs. machine layer** — ground facts are authored (by people or
gated rounds); the machine layer (Archetype nodes, derived edges like
INSTANCE_OF) is *computed* from ground + schema at every apply. Nobody
authors the machine layer; re-derivation owns it.

**Receipts** — review-evidence properties on authored citizens
(`from_text`, `source`, `grade`): the verbatim quote and provenance
that let a claim be checked. Never rendered into outputs.

### The two schema layers

**Metaontology (the kernel)** — the engine's own vocabulary
(`graph/metaontology.yaml`): the four roots (Concept, Facet,
Provenance, Judgment), Procedure, the Judgment family, the visibility
vocabulary. Project-agnostic — the membership test is "would a kid's
storybook project need it?" Semver'd; changes are **ceremonies**.

**Project ontology** — everything THIS knowledge base holds as its own
schema: its labels, catalogs, relationships — living ON the graph as
the Archetype stratum. Owner-governed, versioned as a plain revision
number. `graph/ontology.yaml` is bootstrap provenance for a
from-sources corpus; a corpus born graph-native never has one.

**Ceremony** — the deliberate act of changing the kernel: explicit
owner ruling, a Decision row naming it, the version bump and ledger
line in the same change set. Never casual, never a side effect. The
**schema ceremony** is its project-layer sibling: five permitted
change classes riding an ordinary gated round, itemized in the delta
report's marked section — approving that round IS the ruling.

**Born graph-native** — a knowledge base seeded from the kernel alone
(`python -m graph init`): no bootstrap files, no sources; its project
layer starts empty and grows through gated rounds.

**Label birth** — the schema-ceremony class that grows an empty
project layer: a new spec-carrying label arriving with its
declaration, permitted only while nothing yet sits underneath it.

### Rounds — how canon changes

**Round** — the unit of canon change: cut scratch → author → delta →
gates → apply. Nothing reaches canon any other way.

**Scratch** — a working database cloned from canon where agents author
freely. Wiped and re-cut per round; mistakes here cost nothing.

**Base pin** — cutting scratch records canon's content identity. If
canon moves mid-round, the apply refuses by name — no round lands on a
base that shifted under it.

**Branch** — an independent line of truth WITHIN a KB: born from a
declared base (schema-only today; clone-of-canon is the designed
future base), with its own authoring
copy, ceremony, and chained log, physically unable to write the KB's
live canon, adopted only by the owner's succession ceremony — never a
flag. Pinned base + delta is the contract; the clone is an
implementation detail. A **Pocket Universe ("Pocket")** is the
world-level correlation of branches — one per member KB the work
mutates, read-pins for the rest, landing at one collated gate with
verify-all-before-apply-any extended across every member KB.

**Delta / proposal** — the itemized changeset: scratch minus base,
linted (machine layers refuse authorship), rendered as a report. Its
content hash IS the proposal's identity.

**Plan gate / diff gate** — the two owner gates: the plan gate rules
on intent before authoring; the diff gate rules on the itemized delta
before anything lands. Consent binds to mutation.

**Approve → canonize --apply** — the approval freezes the proposal by
hash; the apply replays exactly that changeset: verify everything
before writing anything, re-derive the machine layer, re-export the
backup, chain the event log.

**Event log & inverse** — one chained, tamper-evident line per applied
round, with the delta's executable inverse recorded — every round can
be walked back.

**Stitch** — the same-round-endpoints mechanism: ground edges whose
target is born by this round's own schema edit ride a declared stitch
file, covered by the same approval, landing after re-derivation births
their endpoints.

**Rederive** — schema-bootstrap maintenance: recompute the machine
layer against the current schema, refusing if ground would change.

**Sitting** — an owner session that rules on a collated sheet of
questions in one pass, rule-by-exception welcome.

**Opening move** — every round's first duty: pay the previous round's
debts (stamp its PR onto its Judgment rows, land its deferred edges).

### The Judgment stratum

**Question / Decision / Answer / Opinion / Requirement / TODO** — the
kernel's ruling vocabulary, all citizens: something open; a ruling made
(by whom, when — supersession expected); a clarification; an agent's
judgment with confidence (junior until ratified); a binding constraint;
work pending. **Approved Omission / Approved Difference** — editorial
rulings the parity judge consults: this absence (or this changed
rendering) is blessed and passes forever. **Verbatim** — a passage
pinned to carry word-for-word; the stored bytes are the truth, the
normalized form is only a matching key.

### Quality machinery

**Parity** — the regeneration bar, owner-ruled: nothing lost, nothing
invented, nothing distorted; presentation free. The **judge** compares
claims mechanically and returns verdicts (matched, omitted, invented,
distorted); reds name themselves.

**Attribution** — the other half of the triangle: every claim in a
draft must find its home in canon. **Parity proves draft ≡ original;
attribution proves draft ⊆ canon** — and a claim that passes parity
but has no home is a hole in *canon*, found automatically.

**The ladder (rungs)** — how strong a claim's home is: **first-class**
(a citizen's structured properties, edges, or Step lifts carry the
fact), **receipt** (found in a citizen's carried sentence quotes),
**soup / prose-only** (found only inside long prose — an honest home
AND a named debt). The rung rides the verdict as its confidence.

**Census** — decomposing an artifact into claims and attributing every
one. **Fact grain** — the ruled claim size: one atomic assertion
("Mary gave Arthur an apple" is three claims).

**Soup map** — the census's output read as a debt map: which sections'
facts are structured citizens and which still live as prose blobs.
The prioritized worklist for ingestion.

**Gap vs. invention** — a homeless claim splits on parity: the
original says it → canon gap (a debt; shipping never stops); parity
called it invented → a named red, presented with the artifact, never
hidden. **Phantom gap** — a "gap" the matcher couldn't see was already
home; **laundering** is removing phantoms from the worklist by reading
structure, not just text.

**Corpus** — the ledger of floors (`graph/corpus/floors.jsonl`) plus
the command that re-checks them all; a deleted guard reds as "the
guard is gone," naming the blessing it orphaned.

**Tripwire** — a test that exists to refuse a specific forgetting: the
schema-version ledger, the roster check, the vocabulary leak. When a
tripwire reds, it worked.

### Runs and margins

**Run / trace** — one casting of agents against a brief, its record
kept as a run-scoped judgment graph: who was cast, what they were
told, what they consulted, what they judged. Claims about runs cite
traces; recollection is not a source.

**Margin** — the system's own annotations on an artifact, span-anchored
(the quote re-locates if the text moves): low-confidence calls,
uncertainties, questions. The owner replies in the same margin; the
reply threads to the Opinion it answers.

**Earned citation** — strong-form attribution: a citation counts when
the cited citizen appears in the drafter's trace. Right-answer-wrong-
path re-derives invisibly.

**Park, never die** — a blocked or interrupted run keeps its state and
resumes; the owner never has to say "try again."

### Lenses — who sees what

**Visibility Class** — a named set of graph elements; the only unit
permissions speak about. Kind **knowledge** (assume-deny: hidden
unless granted) or **masking** (assume-allow: removed only when a mask
names it).

**Visibility Group** — a subject of sight; individuals are size-1
groups; groups nest. (Named "Visibility Group" because a knowledge
base may need the plain word "Group" for its own domain.)

**Verdict** — an authored ALLOWED or DENIED between a group and a
class; denies target flat classes only.

**Fold / lens** — the fold is a subject's transitive group set; the
lens is that fold compiled into what they may see, enforced on the
in-memory graph itself so edges never dangle and derived layers
recompute under it. **Activation** — wearing a subset of your groups
this session; exiting a Pocket is a lens subtraction, not a
membership edit.

**Super admin** — no lens applied. Not a subject with every grant — the
absence of filtering.

**Redacted refusal** — the subject-facing answer for anything hidden:
one uniform "Nothing by that name that you can see." Candid
explanations are a curator privilege.

**Sealed reading** — intake's first phase: comprehend the artifact on
its own terms (kernel allowed, project canon forbidden) before any
mapping, so canon can't bias the reading. **Mapping phase** — then
each artifact-local claim is judged against canon: same-as / extends /
new / contradicts, every mapping a recorded Opinion.

### Campaign terms

**Re-ingest** — the declared milestone: rebuild canon clean from the
published knowledge base, rulings carried, the census as the ruler.

**Succession** — the original remains the parity reference until
the owner *explicitly* declares otherwise. No milestone implies it.

**Wave** — one gated slice of a campaign, sized by the worklist,
closed at a diff gate.

# Lenses: the visibility system

Status: designed in owner dialogue, slice 1 implemented.
The owner opened with two draft approaches and four target uses; a
deep prior-art survey (Zanzibar/SpiceDB/OpenFGA, Neo4j's own RBAC,
Datomic filtered databases, Dolt/TerminusDB/lakeFS, Postgres RLS,
Cedar/XACML/OPA, and the game-design knowledge record) tested them; the owner
supplied the Griptape Nodes fold-down system as a working reference;
the composite below is what survived. Trace tags: [owner] marks the
owner's rulings; [record] marks conclusions the prior art forced.

## Reading the diagram

- **Three lifelines, read top to bottom.** What passes directly
  between submitter and machinery is material and notice — artifacts
  in, the reading shown back, escalations surfacing, answers out. Every
  *decision* crosses through the middle column, the gates — that is
  the point.
- **The plan gate** ratifies *the reading*: how the artifact was
  understood — its structure, what each span is (table, procedure,
  rule-prose, carried flavor), and any concepts the mapping wants to
  create. Nothing about the reading is fait accompli; the machine's
  understanding is reviewable before it becomes work.
- **The diff gate** ratifies *the change*: every fact, beside the
  sentence it came from, with the blast radius named (whose work it
  touches, who gets notified). The convergence loop delivers to this
  gate only what agents could not resolve themselves — the submitter
  never sees finding 3 of 64; they see "these need your word."
- **The machinery's stations, in a phrase each**: *fingerprint & keep*
  — recognize the artifact forever and preserve the original untouched;
  *reading room* — understand its structure and what each piece claims;
  *scratch mapping* — translate the reading into canon's own
  vocabulary (the judgment step); *proposal* — bundle the changes,
  frozen by content; *convergence loop* — regenerate cold, judge
  against the original, burn down every finding agents can fix;
  *approval freeze* — record the ruling, by name, against exactly what
  was reviewed; *apply* — replay exactly what was approved or nothing;
  *event log* — archive the change and its undo, chained so history
  cannot be quietly rewritten; *serve* — answer from canon, cited,
  scoped to the asker.
- **The Pocket** (upper lane) is deliberately gateless: anyone can make
  a copy, experiment, interrogate, and discard. Canon is untouchable
  from inside a Pocket; a proposal carries only what the submitter chose
  to keep.
- **After canon** (Serve → Live with canon), the relationship
  inverts: the submitter asks and the machinery answers — scoped to
  their clearance, cited to its sources, in the medium the evidence
  lives in (images shown, audio played, video cued to the moment). A
  new question that canon cannot answer often becomes the next
  artifact — the loop's re-entry.

## Slice 1 (built) and what waits

Built: graph/lens.py (declarations, fold, compile, apply, explain,
require — pure logic over the in-memory graph value), the lens-scoped
export, the keeper walkthrough as an executable test, floors for the
coherence and flat-deny rules. Declarations rode a YAML surface until
the residence ceremony landed them as citizens; the file surface
retired in the YAML-cleansing arc — the graph is the only
declaration surface, read by declarations_from_graph.

Built in slice 2 (session activation): compile_lens takes the hats
worn this session — subject as one group or an iterable of groups
(each closed upward through its own containers), and `without=` to
subtract named groups after the fold. "Exit the branch" is a
lens subtraction, no membership edit; an empty active set is honest
assume-deny, never an error.

**The residence ceremony was RULED and landed** (owner: "go for it",
after the Griptape Nodes expressibility check — the
model expresses the owner's node-library permissions system with zero
kernel additions; hierarchy as overlapping memberships, posture as
class-kind choice). At the kernel ceremony: **Visibility Group**
and **Visibility Class** join as concepts — named Visibility Group,
not Group, because boundary rule 6 caught the bare name colliding with
a knowledge base's own domain concept: the kernel never claims a word
a project's domain may need. The edge vocabulary
(MEMBER_OF, IN_CLASS, ALLOWED, DENIED flat-only, INCLUDES, MANAGES) is
admitted by the ceremony's Decision row; specs land with first
consumers. The project ontology binds both labels as
implicit delta-born citizens, the Requirement pattern. The engine
grew declarations_from_graph (one lint, two surfaces), the
fold-touching self-visibility in compile_lens (the A/B/C case: you
see your hats and the doors they open; the roster hides by edge
coherence), and the uniform refusal surface (REDACTED_REFUSAL — one
shared string; candid explain is the curator surface). The residence
round (the judgment masking class as the first Visibility Class
citizen + the ruling Decision rows) rides the ordinary
delta/approve/canonize path.

The meta-rule is fully ruled (all four questions + the deferred
developer tier); belief divergence is parked on the owner's word;
MANAGES enforcement is held for multi-user.

The original proposal, kept for the record:

  Kernel (metaontology.yaml), two concepts by the Procedure precedent:

      Group:
        instance_of: Concept
        doc: A subject of visibility. Individuals are size-1 groups;
          groups nest. The fold of a subject's groups is what a lens
          compiles from.
      Visibility Class:
        instance_of: Concept
        doc: A named set of graph elements that visibility verdicts
          speak about — the only permission-bearing unit. kind is
          knowledge (assume-deny) or masking (assume-allow).

  Ground edge vocabulary (authored, never derived): MEMBER_OF
  (Group → Group, the nesting), IN_CLASS (any element → Visibility
  Class, the membership), ALLOWED / DENIED (Group → Visibility
  Class, the verdicts — denies flat-only, enforced by the lint),
  INCLUDES (Visibility Class → Visibility Class, knowledge
  grant-inheritance). Class kind and the label/type selectors ride as
  properties on the Visibility Class citizen. After the ceremony:
  lenses.yaml's content lands as citizens via an ordinary canon
  round, lens.py grows a from-graph declarations reader beside the
  YAML one, and the intake seal becomes physically enforceable.
- **Belief divergence** [deliberately open]: a lens over canon cannot
  represent a subject believing something now false (the roguelike
  map-memory / Dwarf Fortress rumor record: knowledge is a stale
  copy, not a filter). If wanted, that is per-agent overlay data — a
  different mechanism, deferred by name.
- **The meta-rule**: who may see the visibility declarations
  themselves (who-can-see-who-can-see-what) — one rule, wanted before
  multi-user.
- Physical seal enforcement for intake's sealed-reading phase rides
  this system once declarations live on the graph.

## The diagram ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor S as The Submitter participant G as The Two Gates participant M as The Machinery S->>M: drop artifacts — one or many
(docs, tables, images, audio, video) Note over M: fingerprint & keep each original untouched
reading room: structure, spans, content classes M->>S: "here's what I understood —
and how sure I am of each piece" loop until the reading is right S->>M: corrections, in your words M->>S: the reading, revised end S->>G: PLAN GATE — "read it that way" G->>M: the ratified reading Note over M: scratch mapping → proposal, frozen by content opt play first, commit later S->>S: Pocket copy — experiment, interrogate,
discard without trace end loop convergence — until nothing lacks a ruling Note over M: regenerate cold, judge against the originals,
burn down every finding agents can fix M->>S: escalations only — "these need your word" S->>G: rulings, recorded by name G->>M: approved omissions, carried text,
resolved contradictions end S->>G: DIFF GATE — "approve exactly this change?" G->>M: the approval, recorded by name Note over M: apply exactly what was approved, or nothing
event log: change + undo, chained history M->>S: answers — cited, scoped to your clearance,
in the medium the evidence lives in S->>M: the next artifacts — the loop begins again ```

## The keeper walkthrough (the design's acceptance story) [owner]

A keeper named Bramble must know where the hidden Emberstone lies —
but only while the owner works in one workspace branch. Order of
events: cut the branch (readability creator-only — the branch IS the
isolation); author the Emberstone fact and its Emberstone Lore class
membership in the branch; author the grant (Bramble × Emberstone Lore)
→ allow in the branch — the grant is itself branch content, so
"temporary permission" needs no mechanism at all; ask "what does
Bramble know?" inside the branch (the branch selects the reality,
Bramble's folded lens filters within it — she knows Universal + Keeper
knowledge + the Emberstone; other keepers do not); exit the branch
(view returns to canon, where there is nothing to know); land it via
the ordinary delta round (fact, class, grant become canon rows) or
discard the branch clean.

# The north-star workflow — two lanes, two touches

*One diagram: the submitter's lane on top, the machinery's lane beneath.
The north star's whole argument is that the two lanes exchange material
at the ends — the artifact flows in at the drop, answers flow back out at
the close — but exchange *decisions* at exactly two conversations: the
plan gate and the diff gate. Everything else the machinery does happens
without the submitter needing to know it exists. That both gates are
always present here is the mutating-job case of the agentic approach's
engagement signals — an ingest always disambiguates and always mutates;
the reconciliation is recorded once in [agentic-etl.md](agentic-etl.md)
(Invariant 6).*

## The one-paragraph design (owner-accepted)

Nodes and edges join named VISIBILITY CLASSES — the only
permission-bearing unit, since instances are too many to name;
individuals are size-1 GROUPS, groups nest, and verdicts are authored
on (group × class) pairs — additive allows by default, denies legal
only against flat class sets, posture fixed per lens KIND (knowledge
lenses assume-deny, masking lenses assume-allow) rather than
switchable; a LENS is the fold-down of a subject's groups compiled
into a derived resource set — machine layer, never authored — and is
enforced as a filter at the element-access layer of the in-memory
graph value (traversal never yields a masked element, so edges,
paths, aggregates, and re-derivation stay coherent by construction),
with an EXPLAIN operation that re-evaluates unfolded to name the
blocking group, consumers declaring the lenses they REQUIRE or AFFORD
so misconfiguration refuses at build time, super-admin defined as NO
LENS APPLIED, and lens-scoped EXPORTS as the one place lenses
materialize (the shipped runtime graph); Pocket Universes stay out of
the permission model entirely — they are branches on the existing
scratch/delta/canonize machinery, with permissions owning only branch
READABILITY (creator-only by default), and canonize re-tags class
membership as work becomes canon.

## What each lane never sees

The submitter never sees: fingerprints, content hashes, deltas,
inverses, chain verification, content classes, scratch databases. Those
words appear in the lower lane only.

The machinery never decides: what counts as flavor, whether an omission
is acceptable, how a contradiction resolves, when an experiment becomes
a proposal, what a Theme means. Those are ruling verbs, and every one
is recorded with the ruler's name.

## Why each piece (the dialogue, condensed)

- **Classes, not instances** [record]: the owner's Approach A
  (subject-side ACLs) and Approach B (resource-side sets) are duals;
  every surveyed system authors subject-side and ANSWERS list-shaped
  questions resource-side, compiled (Zanzibar's Leopard index, OPA
  partial evaluation, the owner's own Griptape fold-down). A authors;
  B serves; B is derived, never authored — the project's existing
  authored-vs-machine doctrine applied to permissions.
- **Deny discipline** [record]: deny × nested groups is where the
  record draws hard lines (OpenFGA refuses recursive-membership ×
  exclusion at model-build time; AuthZed: "start with no access and
  build up"). Denies here are leaf verdicts against FLAT classes only.
  The owner's tri-state No-Opinion survives — it is what makes
  "the deny didn't match" and "nothing said anything" distinguishable
  (Neo4j's documented fail-open deny is the cautionary tale).
- **Posture per lens kind, never a global switch** [record + owner]:
  no security system surveyed ships switchable assume-allow (XACML's
  configurable algebra is its least-loved feature; the field drifted
  to Cedar's fixed default-deny) — but the game-design record runs the other
  way (fog of war, roguelike map memory are assume-allow with
  carve-outs). Both are right in their kind: knowledge lenses
  assume-deny; masking lenses assume-allow.
- **Enforcement at the element-access layer** [record]: front-door
  result stripping leaks whatever was computed over hidden data
  (counts, path existence — the Postgres RLS side-channel record);
  query rewriting suits SQL, not arbitrary traversal. Datomic's
  d/filter is the fit: filter the in-memory database VALUE so
  traversal never yields a masked element. Our read path is already
  an immutable GraphData; strip_derived is the ur-lens. Coherence
  rules the approaches missed: an edge is visible only if both
  endpoints are; derived layers RE-DERIVE under the lens, never
  filter through it.
- **Explain from day one** [owner's Griptape lesson + record]: the
  fold loses which-group-blocked; decide on the fold, re-evaluate
  unfolded to explain. Cedar's fixed algebra exists for exactly this
  comprehension property.
- **Super admin = no lens** [record, unanimous]: an enforcement-layer
  bypass (BYPASSRLS, Cedar's implicit default), never a subject
  granted everything — under any-deny-wins a modeled admin loses to
  the first deny, and every new class would have to remember them.
- **Pocket Universes are branches, not permissions** [record + owner]:
  every system whose job is isolated adds-AND-removals with later
  merge is a branch system (TerminusDB does it for a knowledge graph;
  tombstones appear in the record only as internal versioning
  implementation, never as the user-facing permission model — masking
  a removal is intrinsically a deny and imports every deny warning
  into steady state). The scratch round with base pinning and
  delta/canonize IS the branch pattern. Permissions own one small
  thing: who may see that a branch exists and read it (the lakeFS
  stance over Dolt's open reads; creator-only by default). Invitation
  is one authored verdict: (their group × the branch) → allow, read
  or write grade; an invited COLLABORATOR gets no lens, an invited
  PLAYER gets a subject's knowledge lens — branch selects the
  reality, the lens filters within it.
- **The storage contract** [owner concern, ruled]: branch = pinned
  base + delta IS the contract (base.json/delta.json already are it);
  clone, filesystem copy-on-write, and delta-overlay-over-a-shared-
  base are interchangeable implementations. Today's full clone is a
  cache, kept while cheap; the overlay (branches sharing one loaded
  immutable base value, O(delta) each) is the path when canon grows.
- **Neo4j's own RBAC: whole-database gates only** [owner + record]:
  a query-only reader on live canon; per-branch database access for pockets.
  Never label/property/traversal privileges, never DENY rules — the
  record documents static per-DB-user roles, deny-wins composition
  that cannot stack into views, fail-open property denies, and
  planner-invisible performance cliffs. The boundary sentence: Neo4j
  enforces which databases a connection may read or write; the engine
  enforces everything about what is visible within one.
- **Exports are the one materialization** [record]: the shipped
  runtime graph is a lens-scoped export (Unreal's cook: strip
  design-time data at build time, flags on the data). Live lenses
  compute fresh from canon — cached lens views reintroduce stale
  revocation (the New Enemy problem in miniature). The canonical
  backup at graph/export/ is ALWAYS lens-free.
